summary_paragraph: A woman with chronic idiopathic pancreatitis was admitted one day after discharge from an outside hospital, presenting with high fever and transient hypotension. She had discontinued TPN and oral intake due to uncontrolled pain and vomiting, during which aspiration was suspected. Imaging revealed right middle lobe opacities consistent with aspiration pneumonitis, but no pancreatic necrosis or infection source. She was initially treated with IV fluids and broad-spectrum antibiotics due to concern for sepsis, but antibiotics were discontinued after blood cultures showed no growth and she remained afebrile. Pain management was optimized with IV Dilaudid and continuation of her fentanyl patch, while TPN was restarted. She progressed to a clear liquid diet, remained stable, and was discharged home on her prior medications with plans for outpatient follow-up. The episode was attributed to aspiration pneumonitis and ongoing chronic pancreatitis flare.
problems: Pneumonitis due to inhalation of food or vomitus
